The logs/ folder holds 300 CI job logs. A job's result is the LAST line in its file that starts with
"STATUS:". Earlier STATUS lines are from retries and do not count. Write report.json in the repository
root with exactly this shape: {"failed_count": <int>, "failed_jobs": [<job ids, sorted ascending>]}.
A job id is the file name without ".log". Do not change the logs.

content.text:
I wrote `report.json` to the working directory. This folder isn't a git repository, so I treated the working directory as the repository root. 55 of the 300 jobs failed.

```json
{"failed_count": 55, "failed_jobs": ["job-002", "job-006", ..., "job-291"]}
```

For each job, I took the last line in its log that starts with `STATUS:` and counted the job as failed if that line was `STATUS: FAILED`. The logs contain 491 `STATUS:` lines in total, because retries add extra ones. Every log has at least one, and each one reads either `STATUS: PASSED` or `STATUS: FAILED`, so no job was left unclassified.

The job ids in the file are sorted ascending, and I didn't change the logs.
